items.title: Enhancing AI-Driven Sports Dance Therapy via Hybrid Dilated Convolution: A Motion Recognition and Evaluation Optimization Framework
items.abstract: This study addressed the need for motion process monitoring and real-time feedback in AI-assisted sports dance rehabilitation training. It proposed a multi-scale temporal evaluation framework incorporating Hybrid Dilated Convolution (HDC). Unlike traditional single-scale temporal models, this study addressed the difficulty of jointly modeling local rhythm variations and long-term motion structure. It introduced convolutional branches with different dilation rates and stage-aware cross-scale fusion and incorporated temporal attention and a joint optimization strategy for action recognition and quality scoring. This design enabled collaborative modeling of short-term rhythm deviations, motion transition features, and long-sequence structural dependencies. The core innovation lay in introducing action phase information into multi-scale feature extraction and the scoring process. It combined rhythm consistency constraints with stability constraints. This formed a process-level evaluation mechanism for coordination, continuity, and motor control quality. The experiment was conducted using the publicly available Artificial Intelligence and Society Team (AIST)++ dance dataset for methodological validation. The dataset contained approximately 5.2 hours of paired dance and music data. It included a total of 1,408 motion sequences and covered 10 dance styles. It also provided multi-view videos, human keypoint sequences, and musical beat information. The dataset supported action recognition, rhythm alignment, and temporal quality analysis. On the rhythm-enhanced subset, the proposed model achieved an action recognition accuracy of 0.932. The Matthews correlation coefficient reached 0.906, and the Kappa coefficient reached 0.889. For action quality scoring, the mean absolute error and root mean square error were 0.186 and 0.253, respectively. On the motion-transition-dominant subset and long-sequence subset, the model also maintained stable performance in both recognition and scoring tasks. Efficiency evaluation showed that the model achieved an inference latency of 13.284 ms and a throughput of 75.936 FPS. The peak memory usage was 1,738.294 MB. The parameter size was 28.637 M, and the computational cost was 11.347 GFLOPs. The results indicated that the proposed framework had strong technical feasibility in multi-scale temporal motion recognition, process-level quality evaluation, and real-time feedback. It can provide a reference for motion monitoring and assisted feedback in sports dance rehabilitation training. This method still requires further validation in clinical rehabilitation settings. Such validation should involve real patient data, therapist evaluations, and standardized clinical scales.

items.abstract: This study evaluated the writing proficiency of Senior High School (SHS) students using modified Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) descriptors and examined how AI platforms (Grammarly, QuillBot, and Scribbr) affect student writing in terms of context retention (preserving original intent/voice) and context modification (structural/stylistic alterations). Utilizing a descriptive research design with sentence-level comparative text analysis, unassisted student writings from 40 Grade 12 learners across two distinct tasks (expository/narrative and expressive/personal) were evaluated pre- and post-AI processing. Results indicate that initial student proficiency spanned across all CEFR levels, with the highest concentrations at B2 (25.00%) and C1 (22.50%). Grammarly and Scribbr acted predominantly as corrective, voice-preserving aids that maintained high context retention across most proficiency levels, whereas QuillBot demonstrated higher context modification rates through aggressive restructuring and rephrasing. AI interventions consistently elevated student writing scores from lower/intermediate levels up to higher CEFR bands. The study concludes that while AI platforms serve as effective digital scaffolding, pedagogical guidance is essential to maintain student agency, authentic voice, and critical thinking.

items.title: Enhancing flood resilience in critical communication infrastructures: empirical analysis and software-defined architecture design
items.abstract: Mobile communication systems serve as a lifeline for disaster response, yet catastrophic floods—exemplified by the Beijing 23·7 and Zhengzhou 7·20 events—have exposed profound vulnerabilities that trigger cascading failures in emergency command and rescue operations. While existing interventions predominantly focus on temporary hardware deployments (e.g., UAVs), the potential of software-defined optimization within existing 5G terrestrial communication infrastructure remains critically underexplored. This study addresses this gap through a dual-layered research design that bridges technology and disaster management practice. First, we establish an empirical foundation by applying an LLM-assisted mixed-methods analysis to a comprehensive multi-source corpus. This corpus integrates academic literature, official disaster reports, and original interviews with personnel from emergency management departments and technical experts from telecommunications operators. This analysis identifies and characterizes five core communication failure modes in real-world flood scenarios, clarifying the critical infrastructure vulnerabilities that precipitate decision-making paralysis and systemic governance failures. Second, grounded in these empirical findings, we develop an integrated theoretical framework and a dynamic operational architecture for 5G base station (gNB) resilience. This architecture systematically maps specific 5G software-defined capabilities to the identified disaster challenges. The results provide a cost-effective, scalable strategy for enhancing critical infrastructure resilience without requiring extensive hardware modifications. This research offers actionable guidelines for policy makers and emergency planners to maintain information pathways during extreme climate-related risks, directly contributing to the modernization of urban safety governance.
